title: Predictive SLI Targeter & Tranche-based Error-Budget Allocator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we scale Dedicated and Private customers, teams need a deterministic way to allocate limited error budget across releases and coordinated rollouts. Current manual allocations are slow to react and obscure which initiatives should be throttled when SLI degradation occurs.

Goal: Build a predictive SLI targeter that suggests per-initiative SLI targets and automatically assigns error-budget tranches (time-bounded allocations). Integrate with the initiative tracker so rollouts can be auto-throttled or rolled back according to tranche burn signals. Deliver a dashboard that visualizes tranche allocations, burn-rate forecasts, and recommended rollback windows.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive model produces per-initiative SLI target suggestions with confidence bounds (example outputs stored in Confluence).
Tranche allocation engine can create, modify, and revoke error-budget tranches via API and map them to initiative IDs in the tracker.
Dashboard shows live burn-rate, 7-day forecast, and recommended rollback window for each tranche; on-call can trigger suggested rollback with two-click flow.
Automated policy: when tranche forecast crosses 80% burn within 24h, system enforces throttling policy and notifies initiative owners via Slack/Email.
End-to-end test harness simulates SLI regressions and validates rollback runway behavior in staging with <5% false-positive throttle rate.
tasks: PM: finalize tranche allocation rules and success metrics (Aisha)
ENG: prototype predictive SLI model and publish test predictions (ENG-19321)
ENG: implement tranche API (create/update/revoke) and integrate with initiative tracker backend
ENG: add rollout throttle action in Console and wire to tranche state
DX: design dashboard mockups and two-click rollback flow
QA: build simulation harness and smoke tests for rollback policy
OBS: add burn-rate telemetry and alerting rules to reliability-sli topic
updates: 2025-06-12: Kickoff meeting—aligned on tranche concept and three rollout policies (soft-throttle, hard-throttle, rollback). Action: ENG to produce initial model by 2025-06-20.
2025-06-14: Design review—DX approved low-fidelity dashboard; requested clearer escalation path for on-call. Action: PM to draft Slack message templates.

2025-06-16: ENG spike—prototyped an AR(7) ensemble for short-window burn forecasting. Initial precision is promising on historical runbook data but recall needs tuning (see github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/7921).
2025-06-18: Decision: prioritize tranche enforcement API and dashboard read path for MVP; predictive model will ship as 'advisory' in alpha to reduce automation risks.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Automated rollback reduces MTTR but increases risk of false positives. Chosen approach: advisory predictions + automated soft-throttle at 80% forecast; hard rollback requires human confirmation during alpha.
Scope decision: exclude multi-region cross-customer coordinated rollbacks from MVP to reduce blast-radius complexity.
Model tradeoff: simpler statistical models (time-series ensembles) chosen for explainability over black-box deep learning in alpha phase.
Data retention tradeoff: use 30-day sliding window for burn-rate inputs to balance responsiveness vs noise.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False-positive throttles impacting customer SLA. Mitigation: alpha mode = advisory only; soft-throttles are percentage-limited and reversible.
Risk: Missing instrumentation for newly onboarded dedicated pools. Mitigation: ENG to ship required telemetry shim and gate tranche assignment until metrics exist.
Risk: Confusion across multiple initiative owners about tranche ownership. Mitigation: dashboard displays explicit owner & contact and auto-notifications on changes.
notes: We should coordinate with Sales for Dedicated customers who have bespoke SLO contracts — include opt-out in client config.
Consider a follow-up to expose tranche history in audit logs for compliance teams (PII concerns reviewed by Security).
Potential extension: integrate model with Optimize suggestions to recommend quantization or batching changes when persistent burn occurs.
